chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Maymoun, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
The female in Ihram must not wear the niqab, because the Ihram of the woman is in her face, and the Ihram of the man is in his head.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمَةُ: A woman in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Why is a woman in Ihram prohibited from wearing a niqab?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific garment restrictions for women in Ihram, establishing that the face is the primary site of their ritual state, unlike men whose head is the focal point. This distinction is central to Shia fiqh regarding the permissibility of veiling the face while keeping it uncovered for identification and worship. The ruling underscores the principle that Ihram involves removing adornments and specific coverings to signify equality before God.
